text.title: Stocks slide as Nvidia, China chip curbs hit tech; oil falls on Mideast supply
text.summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply, with the S&P 500 down 1.9% and the Nasdaq down 2.5%, as AI and chip shares sold off ahead of Nvidia's earnings. The VIX rose 18.7% to 22.9. Oil dropped 3.9% and Treasury yields slipped.

drivers.t: Technology was the weakest sector, down 3.2%. Micron, AMD and other AI stocks fell as investors worried about Nvidia's results and whether it will scale back financing of the AI ecosystem.

The Commerce Department announced a rule aimed at restricting China's remote access to advanced chips, and Nvidia's stock extended its decline. The S&P 500's drop was its third straight and its sharpest since Nvidia's CEO resigned last week.
Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close, with Jensen Huang's exit looming over the market. The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.7% in what the FT called a gloomy start to a pivotal week for the AI trade.
WTI crude fell 3.9% to $85.09 as Middle East exports recovered and forecasts pointed to a fourth-quarter surplus. Energy shares lost 2.0%.
Treasury yields slipped at the start of the week as Fed Chair Warsh gave no hints about the path of interest rates. The 10-year yield fell 3 bp to 5.1% and the 2-year fell 5 bp to 4.8%.

Customers of Chase, Bank of America and other banks reported service problems. JPMorgan said a temporary software bug was affecting consumer banking, with no indication of bad actors or of multiple banks being affected.
